title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 17.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He placed forces in all the fenced cities
He took away the high places
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat his son reigned
questions.explanation: This statement appears first in the chapter, specifically in 2 Chronicles 17:1.

questions.question: Who reigned after Asa according to 2 Chronicles 17?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead as stated in 2 Chronicles 17:1.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat do to strengthen himself against Israel?
options: He placed forces in all the fenced cities
He took away the high places
questions.correctAnswer: He placed forces in all the fenced cities
questions.explanation: This action is described in 2 Chronicles 17:2.

questions.question: Why was the LORD with Jehoshaphat?
options: He walked in the first ways of David
He took away the high places
questions.correctAnswer: He walked in the first ways of David
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David, as found in 2 Chronicles 17:3.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat seek according to 2 Chronicles 17?
options: The LORD God of his father
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD God of his father
questions.explanation: Jehoshaphat sought to the LORD God of his father, as stated in 2 Chronicles 17:4.

questions.question: What did the LORD do because of Jehoshaphat's ways?
options: Established the kingdom in his hand
Sent him to teach in the cities
questions.correctAnswer: Established the kingdom in his hand
questions.explanation: The verse states that therefore the LORD stablished the kingdom in his hand, as found in 2 Chronicles 17:5.

questions.question: What did all Judah bring to Jehoshaphat?
questions.correctAnswer: Presents
questions.explanation: The verse indicates that all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents, as stated in 2 Chronicles 17:5.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat take away from Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: The high places and groves
questions.explanation: The verse states that he took away the high places and groves out of Judah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 17:6.

questions.question: In which year of his reign did Jehoshaphat send to his princes?
questions.correctAnswer: Third year
questions.explanation: It is stated in 2 Chronicles 17:7 that he sent to his princes in the third year of his reign.

questions.question: Who did Jehoshaphat send to teach in the cities of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Obadiah
questions.explanation: Obadiah is one of the princes that Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 17:7.

questions.question: What did Jehoshaphat's heart become lifted up in?
questions.correctAnswer: The ways of the LORD
questions.explanation: His heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 17:6.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat sought the LORD God of his father.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated in 2 Chronicles 17:4.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat took away the high places and groves out of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 17:6.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat was not concerned with the doings of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not state that Jehoshaphat was unconcerned about Israel's doings; rather, he walked in his commandments and not after them, as noted in 2 Chronicles 17:4.

questions.question: All Judah rebelled against Jehoshaphat.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not indicate that all Judah rebelled; it states that all Judah brought presents to Jehoshaphat, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 17:5.

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were sent by Jehoshaphat to teach in Judah along with the priests Elishama and Jehoram?
options: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, Tobadonijah
questions.correctAnswer: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, Tobadonijah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:8 lists these Levites sent with the priests Elishama and Jehoram to teach in Judah.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 17:10 promise will happen if the Levites and priests teach the people as commanded in 2 Chronicles 17:9?
options: The fear of the LORD will fall upon surrounding kingdoms, preventing war
The cities of Judah will be destroyed
Jehoshaphat will lose his riches and honour
questions.correctAnswer: The fear of the LORD will fall upon surrounding kingdoms, preventing war
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:10 states that because the Levites and priests taught the people, the fear of the LORD fell on neighboring kingdoms, so they made no war against Jehoshaphat.

questions.question: What kind of tribute did the Arabians bring to Jehoshaphat?
options: Seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred he goats
questions.correctAnswer: Seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred he goats
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:11 specifies that the Arabians brought these flocks as tribute to Jehoshaphat.

questions.question: How did Jehoshaphat's building projects relate to his military strength as described in the surrounding verses?
options: He built castles and cities of store while having mighty men of valour in Jerusalem
He neglected military strength to focus only on building cities
He relied solely on foreign allies for protection
He disbanded the army to fund construction
questions.correctAnswer: He built castles and cities of store while having mighty men of valour in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:12 and 17:13 together show Jehoshaphat grew strong by building fortifications and maintaining a powerful army.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from Jehoshaphat sending Levites and priests to teach the law throughout Judah?
options: The importance of teaching and spreading God's word to strengthen faith and community
That only kings should teach religious laws
That laws are unnecessary for spiritual growth
That teaching should be limited to Jerusalem alone
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of teaching and spreading God's word to strengthen faith and community
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:8-9 illustrates how teaching the law widely helped bring reverence to God and peace to the land.

questions.question: How does the fear of the LORD affecting neighboring kingdoms demonstrate a principle for Christian living?
options: Obedience to God brings protection and peace even in difficult circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God brings protection and peace even in difficult circumstances
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:10 shows that reverence for God caused surrounding kingdoms to refrain from war, indicating the protective power of faithfulness.

questions.question: What does the tribute from the Philistines and Arabians suggest about Jehoshaphat's reputation among neighboring peoples?
options: He was respected and recognized as a powerful leader
He was feared and hated universally
He was ignored by other nations
questions.correctAnswer: He was respected and recognized as a powerful leader
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:11 indicates that neighboring peoples brought gifts and tribute, signifying respect and alliance rather than hostility.

questions.question: What spiritual principle can be drawn from Jehoshaphat removing high places and groves from Judah?
options: Removing idolatry strengthens commitment to God
Idolatry is acceptable if done secretly
All worship places are equally valid
questions.correctAnswer: Removing idolatry strengthens commitment to God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:6 shows Jehoshaphat's heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD partly by removing idolatrous sites, demonstrating the need to eliminate false worship.

questions.question: How does Jehoshaphat's reliance on God's ways rather than Baalim reflect on Christian integrity?
options: Faithful obedience to God over cultural pressures maintains spiritual integrity
Compromise with false beliefs is necessary
questions.correctAnswer: Faithful obedience to God over cultural pressures maintains spiritual integrity
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:3 highlights Jehoshaphat's choice to walk in God's ways instead of Baalim, showing the importance of steadfastness in faith.

questions.question: Why is it significant that Jehoshaphat set garrisons not only in Judah but also in cities of Ephraim?
options: Strengthening defenses in strategic locations promotes peace and security
It was a waste of resources
It was a sign of distrust in God
questions.correctAnswer: Strengthening defenses in strategic locations promotes peace and security
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:2 shows Jehoshaphat's strategic placement of forces to maintain security, illustrating wisdom in stewardship and protection.

questions.question: What can be learned from Jehoshaphat’s heart being lifted up in the ways of the LORD?
options: Delighting in God’s ways leads to righteous reforms and blessings
Pride in one's own ways is preferable
Ignoring God’s commands results in prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Delighting in God’s ways leads to righteous reforms and blessings
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:6 describes Jehoshaphat’s heart lifted up in the ways of the LORD, motivating him to remove idolatry and receive blessings.

questions.question: How does maintaining mighty men of valour in Jerusalem relate to spiritual leadership?
options: Physical preparedness supports spiritual leadership and protection of the community
Spiritual leaders should avoid military involvement
Might and valor are irrelevant in faith
Only prayer is necessary for protection
questions.correctAnswer: Physical preparedness supports spiritual leadership and protection of the community
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:13 shows Jehoshaphat’s strong army as part of his leadership, highlighting balance between faith and practical defense.

questions.question: What does the number of mighty men of valour under Adnah suggest about Jehoshaphat's military organization?
options: It was vast and well-structured by family houses
It consisted mostly of foreign mercenaries
questions.correctAnswer: It was vast and well-structured by family houses
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:14 lists captains and thousands of men according to their families, indicating a large, organized military force.

questions.question: Jehoshaphat's sending of princes to teach in the cities of Judah in his third year is an example of what Christian principle?
options: Delegating responsibility to promote spiritual education
Centralizing all teaching in one place
questions.correctAnswer: Delegating responsibility to promote spiritual education
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:7 shows Jehoshaphat sending leaders to teach, illustrating the importance of shared responsibility in faith instruction.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoshaphat's reign was marked by the removal of idolatrous sites in Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:6 states that Jehoshaphat took away the high places and groves, removing idolatry from Judah.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 17.

questions.question: Who was the captain next to Adnah, and how many mighty men of valour did he have with him?
options: Jehohanan, with two hundred and fourscore thousand
Jehozabad, with one hundred and fourscore thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Jehohanan, with two hundred and fourscore thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:15 states that next to Adnah was Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred and fourscore thousand.

questions.question: Which captain willingly offered himself unto the LORD and led two hundred thousand mighty men of valour?
questions.correctAnswer: Amasiah the son of Zichri
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:16 identifies Amasiah son of Zichri as the one who willingly offered himself unto the LORD and commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valour.

questions.question: Of which tribe was Eliada, and how many armed men with bow and shield were with him?
options: Benjamin; one hundred and eighty thousand
Judah; two hundred and fourscore thousand
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin; two hundred thousand
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:17 states Eliada was of Benjamin and had two hundred thousand armed men with bow and shield.

questions.question: Who was the captain with one hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for war?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehozabad
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:18 names Jehozabad as the captain with one hundred and fourscore thousand ready prepared for war.

questions.question: What role did the captains and their men have in relation to the king besides those in the fenced cities throughout Judah?
options: They were sent as ambassadors to Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They waited on the king
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:19 explains these captains and their men waited on the king, besides those whom the king put in the fenced cities throughout Judah.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 17:19, what is the significance of the king putting men in the fenced cities throughout Judah?
options: To strengthen defenses throughout the kingdom
To build temples in every city
questions.correctAnswer: To strengthen defenses throughout the kingdom
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:19, together with verse 2, shows that the king placed garrisons in fenced cities to strengthen Judah's defenses.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'gibbor' (גִּבּוֹר) in 2 Chronicles 17:16 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Mighty man of valour
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'gibbor' used in 2 Chronicles 17:16 means 'mighty man of valour,' describing a warrior or heroic figure.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in the listing of captains and their troops in 2 Chronicles 17:14-19?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: The passage uses parallelism by repeating a similar structure in listing captains with their number of men, as seen in 2 Chronicles 17:14-19.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God establishing the king's kingdom because he sought the LORD, as in 2 Chronicles 17:5?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Kings 3:6
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:6 echoes the theme of a king seeking the LORD and God establishing his kingdom, similar to 2 Chronicles 17:5 where the LORD stablished Jehoshaphat's kingdom.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of God’s kingdom being established through walking in the ways of God from 2 Chronicles 17:3-4?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 5:6
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:6, 'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness,' fulfills the theme from 2 Chronicles 17:3-4 of walking in God's commandments and seeking Him.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the listing of the captains and their mighty men in 2 Chronicles 17:14?
options: Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built castles and cities of store
The fear of the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms around Judah
Levites and priests were sent to teach the law in Judah
Jehoshaphat placed forces in all fenced cities of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built castles and cities of store
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:13, immediately preceding verse 14, says Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built in Judah castles and cities of store.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jehoshaphat sending Levites and priests to teach the law in the cities of Judah as described in 2 Chronicles 17:7-9?
options: It reflects a religious reform to strengthen covenant faithfulness
It was a strategy to prepare for war
It was to collect taxes more effectively
It was to establish trade agreements
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects a religious reform to strengthen covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:7-9 shows Jehoshaphat’s effort to teach the law and promote covenant faithfulness, indicating religious reform.

questions.question: How does the structure of 2 Chronicles 17 exhibit an inclusio literary device?
options: By opening and closing with Jehoshaphat’s reign and military strength
By repeating the same phrase in every verse
By using parallelism only in the middle section
By focusing only on one tribe
questions.correctAnswer: By opening and closing with Jehoshaphat’s reign and military strength
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17 begins with Jehoshaphat strengthening his reign and ends with detailing his military captains and forces, framing the chapter as an inclusio.

questions.question: Does 2 Chronicles 17:10 indicate that the fear of the LORD caused surrounding kingdoms to avoid war with Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:10 explicitly states that the fear of the LORD fell upon all neighboring kingdoms, causing them to make no war against Jehoshaphat.

questions.question: Is it true that Jehoshaphat removed the Levites from teaching the law in Judah as part of his reforms in 2 Chronicles 17?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:7-9 describes Jehoshaphat sending Levites and priests to teach the law, not removing them.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 17:3 teach about God's relationship with the faithful?
options: God is with those who walk in His ways and avoid idolatry
God only blesses those who perform sacrifices
God favors Israel exclusively over Judah
God's presence is conditional on military success
questions.correctAnswer: God is with those who walk in His ways and avoid idolatry
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:3 states, 'And the LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim,' indicating God's presence accompanies obedience and rejection of idolatry.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in 2 Chronicles 17:6?
options: Sanctification involves removing idols and false worship
Sanctification is solely a matter of internal belief
Sanctification is not necessary for kings
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves removing idols and false worship
questions.explanation: Verse 6 describes Jehoshaphat taking away 'the high places and groves out of Judah,' showing sanctification includes active removal of idolatrous practices.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning the means of grace is taught in 2 Chronicles 17:9?
options: Teaching the law of the LORD is a primary means of spiritual instruction
Spiritual growth depends only on personal revelation
Levitical teaching was optional for the people
The law was kept secret from the common people
questions.correctAnswer: Teaching the law of the LORD is a primary means of spiritual instruction
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains that Levites and priests went about teaching the book of the law of the LORD, emphasizing the importance of scriptural instruction in sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 17:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 17:5 states, 'Therefore the LORD stablished the kingdom in his hand,' showing God's sovereign control over the establishment of earthly kingdoms.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by 2 Chronicles 17:10 where surrounding kingdoms fear the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: The fear of the LORD described in verse 10 reflects God's holiness, which causes reverence and awe among the nations.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 17:1–2 prepare for the theme of covenant faithfulness found later in Scripture?
options: By showing the importance of political and military strength aligned with obedience to God
By emphasizing isolationism from Israel and other nations
By focusing on economic prosperity as a sign of covenant blessing
By advocating for religious syncretism to maintain peace
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the importance of political and military strength aligned with obedience to God
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 2 describe Jehoshaphat strengthening Judah militarily while walking in God's ways, prefiguring later biblical themes where covenant faithfulness brings divine blessing and security.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 17:11 relate to the broader biblical theme of Gentile tribute to God's chosen king?
options: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles in God’s kingdom through submission
It shows Gentiles always opposed Israel without exception
It illustrates that tribute is only material and not spiritual
It demonstrates the futility of political alliances
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the inclusion of Gentiles in God’s kingdom through submission
questions.explanation: Verse 11 records Philistines and Arabians bringing tribute, symbolizing Gentile recognition and submission to God's anointed king, a motif fulfilled in the New Testament.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 7 and 9 teach about the role of Scripture and teaching in sanctification?
options: Scriptural teaching by appointed leaders is essential for the spiritual growth of the people
Sanctification is independent of external teaching
Only priests but not Levites are responsible for teaching
The law was meant to be hidden from most people
questions.correctAnswer: Scriptural teaching by appointed leaders is essential for the spiritual growth of the people
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 9 describe Jehoshaphat sending princes with Levites and priests to teach the law throughout Judah, affirming the doctrine that sanctification requires authoritative instruction in God's Word.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do verses 3 and 4 provide about human sin and God's covenant faithfulness?
options: Faithfulness to God’s covenant and rejection of idolatry leads to divine presence and blessing
Human sin is irrelevant if one claims Davidic descent
Seeking Baalim is compatible with covenant faithfulness
God’s blessing is arbitrary and not linked to human obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness to God’s covenant and rejection of idolatry leads to divine presence and blessing
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 emphasize Jehoshaphat’s walking in David’s ways and not seeking Baalim but the LORD, showing covenant faithfulness results in God's favor despite human sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine provision and human responsibility is taught by combining verses 5 and 12?
options: God establishes the kingdom, but human effort in administration and building is required
Human effort alone secures prosperity without God’s involvement
Divine provision eliminates the need for human work
Prosperity is unrelated to either divine or human action
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes the kingdom, but human effort in administration and building is required
questions.explanation: Verse 5 shows God establishing Jehoshaphat’s kingdom and verse 12 notes his building projects, teaching a cooperation between divine providence and human responsibility.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 17:7-9 promotes a legalistic religion that neglects grace. What does the passage actually teach?
options: It teaches the necessity of instructing the people in God's law as part of covenant faithfulness, not legalism
It commands salvation by works alone
It forbids any reliance on grace for justification
It implies that priests' teaching replaces the Holy Spirit's work
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the necessity of instructing the people in God's law as part of covenant faithfulness, not legalism
questions.explanation: Verses 7–9 describe sending Levites and priests to teach the law, emphasizing faithful obedience and instruction within the covenant, without denying grace-based salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine about human valor and divine empowerment is taught in 2 Chronicles 17:14?
options: Human valor is recognized but ultimately under divine empowerment
Military might alone is sufficient for divine favor
Valor is irrelevant to God's purposes
Only spiritual leaders matter in God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: Human valor is recognized but ultimately under divine empowerment
questions.explanation: Verse 14 lists mighty men of valor with their numbers, but earlier verses show God’s presence with Jehoshaphat, indicating human strength functions under divine empowerment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by 2 Chronicles 17:10 in causing fear among neighboring kingdoms?
questions.correctAnswer: Power
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states the fear of the LORD fell upon surrounding kingdoms, demonstrating God's powerful presence that deters war.

questions.question: How do verses 2 and 19 together illustrate the relationship between centralized and decentralized authority in God's kingdom?
options: Jehoshaphat places forces both in the king's presence and in fenced cities, showing a balance of centralized and delegated authority
All authority is centralized exclusively in the king's court
Military power is decentralized without kingly oversight
The king relinquishes control to local authorities completely
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoshaphat places forces both in the king's presence and in fenced cities, showing a balance of centralized and delegated authority
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes garrisons in cities, and verse 19 notes men waiting on the king besides those in cities, showing a governance structure combining central and regional control.

questions.question: What theological theme is developed by comparing 2 Chronicles 17:4 and 17 regarding covenant obedience and teaching?
options: Obedience to God's commandments requires intentional teaching and dissemination of His law
Teaching is unnecessary if the king is obedient
Covenant obedience is an internal matter only, unrelated to public instruction
Israel's customs should be imitated over God's law
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's commandments requires intentional teaching and dissemination of His law
questions.explanation: Verse 4 notes Jehoshaphat's obedience to God's commandments and verse 7 shows he sends officials to teach, linking obedience with active instruction.
